thread:
maya: FYI AcmePay opened a ticket — their prod dashboard shows tokens/sec going negative starting ~09:15 PST. TTFT also jumping around. Screenshot attached.

support-bot: New ticket #INC-5421 created for AcmePay. Priority: high.

john: Is this only the console visualization or is the raw streaming aggregate showing negatives too?

maya: I asked them to run the internal query, they pasted a snippet:
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS minute, sum(tokens) - lag(sum(tokens)) OVER (ORDER BY minute) AS delta_tokens
FROM streaming_events
WHERE customer_id = 'acmepay' AND ts >= '2026-03-05 08:00:00'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute DESC
```
Results show: -1200, -980, -1024 for several recent windows.

alyssa: Oof. That looks like a delta calculation produced negative deltas. Could be event order flips, a counter reset/wrap, or a bug in the rollup job. Any recent deploys to the streaming-aggregator?

kevin: I rolled out streaming-aggregator v2.14 last night at 02:10 UTC. The change touched the delta calc when batches span partitions. Rolling back now to confirm.

sre-bot: deploy-started streaming-aggregator v2.14 by kevin at 02:10 UTC.

john: Meanwhile can someone check raw event counts for a small time window to see if source increments actually go down? Run: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://int-metrics/api/v1/events?customer=acmepay&from=2026-03-05T09:10:00Z&to=2026-03-05T09:20:00Z" | jq '.events[] | {ts: .ts, tokens: .tokens}'
```

maya: I ran that; raw events monotonic increasing per event, no negatives, per-event tokens look fine. The negative deltas only show up after our windowed aggregation.

alyssa: Could be an off-by-one in how we apply lag() across partition boundaries — the earlier window used the last row of previous partition but now it's resetting lag to 0. If new code subtracts current - previous and previous is NULL or zero in certain race conditions, it could flip sign due to data types.

kevin: Quick check: the v2.14 change switched delta from unsigned to signed 32-bit in the in-memory buffer to support temporary negatives for reconciliation. I wonder if the rollup combines a signed delta with an unsigned running total and we got an integer wrap when casting.

john: Good hypothesis. Can you repro locally with a partition boundary test? If so we need a hotfix.

kevin: Repro script attached small run:
```python
# simulate partition boundary
buckets = [1000000000, 2000000000, 3000000000]
# previous total represented as uint32 -> wraps at 2**32
prev = 4294967000  # near wrap
curr = 50
print((curr - prev) & 0xffffffff)  # yields large negative equivalent when interpreted signed
```
Gives a negative-looking delta when misinterpreted.

maya: That matches timeline — AcmePay had a very large cumulative counter (long-running connection). Looks like wrapping on total tokens caused the rollup delta to become negative after type mixing.

alyssa: Action items: (1) roll aggregator v2.13 back (kevin) — done? (2) patch v2.14 to normalize types and detect wrap-around (kevin + eng-runtime) (3) schedule backfill of the bad windows to recalc deltas for affected customers (data-eng) (4) notify AcmePay with workaround and ETA.

kevin: Rolled back to v2.13 at 09:25 PST. Confirming dashboards are re-computing.

sre-bot: deploy-complete streaming-aggregator v2.13 by kevin at 09:25 PST.

john: Console shows tokens/sec back to normal for AcmePay around 09:30. Can we run a backfill job for 09:00–10:00 to correct the bad points?

maya: I've kicked off backfill job BF-765 targeting that hour for affected customers. It will re-run aggregation with corrected logic.

alyssa: Create a follow-up ticket for a safer invariant check: if delta < 0 then check for wrap and attempt correction rather than surface negative to the dashboard. Also add an alert for sustained negative deltas.

maya: Notified AcmePay support channel: explained cause (counter wrap due to type mix) and actions: rollback, backfill in progress, patch ETA ~3 hours. They acknowledged. :thumbsup:

support-bot: INC-5421 updated with root cause, rollback, and BF-765 backfill job.

kevin: Will open PR for v2.14 patch to use 64-bit signed arithmetic for deltas and a wrap-detection guard. PR #4482.

maya: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated when backfill finishes or if AcmePay reports anything else.

kevin: Backfill completed at 10:02 PST, BF-765 done. Confirmed negative points replaced with corrected deltas.

maya: Closing loop with customer now. Marking INC-5421 resolved pending any further noise.

john: Good catch. Let's add a unit test for partition boundary wrap cases so this doesn't regress.

alyssa: Added test to data-eng suite, will land with PR #4482.

maya: Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
